title: Why answers vary
description: What temperature is, and why the same request gives different answers.

steps.text: You ask the same question twice and get two different answers. That's not a glitch. A model has some randomness built in, and a setting called temperature controls it.

Remember: a model produces text one word at a time, each time choosing the next word from many options with different chances. Temperature decides how boldly it moves away from the most likely option.

steps.caption: The numbers are an example: a real model has thousands of options. Move the slider and drag a word

steps.text: Low temperature: the model almost always takes the most likely option. Answers are predictable, steady, close to repeating themselves. That's good for facts, code and instructions — where you need accuracy, not imagination.

High temperature: the model more often picks less obvious words. Answers are more varied and lively, but riskier: more unexpected turns and a bigger chance of going off track. That's for ideas, writing and brainstorming.
This is why different runs of the same request differ — and why you can use it: run a question several times and pick the best answer. That has a lesson of its own, “Arena and agent swarms.”

steps.situation: You need to word a precise clause of a contract about payment.
options: Low — you need accuracy and predictability
High — let it word things more boldly
steps.explain: For facts, code and legal wording, spread does harm — keep the answer near the most likely option.

steps.text: Practice. After the lesson, ask me the same creative question twice in a regular chat — for example, “think of a name for a bakery.” Compare the answers: the difference between the runs is temperature at work.

Remember the main point: different answers don't mean “the model contradicts itself.” They are randomness that has been tuned. Need stability? Expect an even tone. Need freshness? Let the spread run wider.

questions.q: Why does the same request give different answers?
options: Word choice has some randomness, which temperature controls
The model forgets its last answer each time and writes anew
A different model from the chain handles the request each time
questions.explain: Temperature sets how far the model moves from the most likely word — that is where the variety comes from.

questions.q: When is low temperature the right choice?
options: When you need accuracy and predictability — facts, code, instructions
When you want creative brainstorming and unexpected ideas
When you want the answer to come out longer and more detailed
questions.explain: Low temperature keeps the answer near the most likely option — it's about accuracy.

questions.q: You asked twice for a bakery name and got different ones. What does that mean?
options: That's how randomness works: you can pick the best run
The model broke and contradicts itself
The first answer was a mistake, and the model fixed it
questions.explain: Spread from temperature makes runs differ, and you can pick the best of them. The arena is built on that — we'll reach it at the end of the course.
